Thinh N
Dear julienpW7066CY,
 
First and foremost, thank you for choosing to dine with us at Aubergine49. We sincerely apologise for your disappointment with your dining experience.
 
We would like to take a moment to address a few points regarding your feedback.
 
Regarding your first point, we quote: 
- "Frozen bread (in a country that makes very good bread, this is quite sad)." 
 
We completely understand your feelings about frozen bread and want to assure you that the bread we serve at Aubergine49 is freshly made and baked.
 
Allow us to share a bit about our chef’s heritage to provide you with a better understanding. Our chef, Chef Thinh, is a third-generation member of a family that has a rich history of owning a bakery (boulangerie) in Hoi An. Chef Thinh’s grandparents were among the few proud bakery owners in Hoi An back in the 1980s and 90s, supplying bread to local stores such as Banh Mi Phuong and The Queen of Banh Mi, Madam Khanh (who were not well-known at that time).
 
Growing up in the Old Town of Hoi An, Chef Thinh has cherished memories of how bread was made with true artisan love and care. Bakers would start their shifts at midnight to prepare the dough; by 2 a.m., you could hear the sound of proofed dough slapping against the wooden worktop, creating a rhythmic drumming echoing through the ancient town. The bread was baked in a large wood-fired oven, with a splash of syrup and honey, filling the air with the sweetness of caramelisation and giving the bread its golden coat, both in appearance and flavour. Chef Thinh’s uncles and aunts still own well-known bakeries in town today.
 
Regarding the wine, it appears there was a misunderstanding. You commented: 
- "The wine pairing is quite bad with vented wines, as they do not keep the opened bottles (for the red wine) in good condition. The waiters unfortunately have no idea about wine tasting, which makes the experience very unpleasant (they refused to open a new bottle)."
 
From our understanding, you ordered a three-course set meal but wished to accompany it with the wine pairings from the five-course degustation menu, which is uncommon, as the flavours may not match. However, we are always happy to accommodate our clients' needs. We assure you that the wine is stored at the correct temperature for red wine (between 15°C - 18°C), and opened bottles are vacuum-sealed to maintain their quality. The bottle of French Syrah served to you that night was nearly full, with only one small glass poured from it, and it met our standards. However, it seemed you did not enjoy it and requested a change. Our waiter, striving to meet your expectations, offered you another French Syrah from a different producer, which we believed would pair well with your meal. Unfortunately, there may have been a miscommunication, as the waiter did not convey this clearly, and you ultimately decided to go back to the Pinot Noir you had previously selected. We do find your comments about our waiter a bit harsh, as he was doing his best to accommodate your requests throughout the entire process.
 
We truly understand your disappointment, and we apologise for not meeting your dining expectations. Your experience matters to us, and we would be grateful for the opportunity to welcome you back to Aubergine49. We are committed to providing you with the exceptional dining experience you deserve.

Best regards,
The Aubergine49 Team.

Hoi An’s fine dining hidden gem!
Mar 2025 • Friends
One can only describe this restaurant as a hidden gem. Blink and your grab driver misses it, but oh my goodness does this restaurant deliver. Not only the best meal we have had in Vietnam but possibly up there in my top 3 ever dining experiences!

Attentive staff are knowledgeable on their chef’s menu and ingredients, explaining each course in detail. Starting with a palate cleanser prior to commencing entre service. The menu selection is comprehensive and the first restaurant in Vietnam able to offer delicious gluten free alternatives. Our party of 7 were delighted with every menu item. If we could have licked out plates we would have! 

This is an absolute must visit restaurant whilst in Hoi An. You are foolish to miss out. We only wish we could have met the chef to congratulate him on our fine dining experience. 

Thank to all the staff who gave us such a lovely evening.

Top 3 dinner experiences of my life
Feb 2025 • Solo
The evening started a bit off due miscommunication, however it was remedied by the Chef Patron himself.

It turned out to be one of the best dining experiences I've ever had:

- Artichoke was beautifully executed, a true piece of art. Delicious and layered as well and introducing to the rest of the experience

- Lobster tail as a 2nd course had a display of a seabed combined with edible "sand" together with colors of a coral reef - simply exquisite

- Oxtail dumpling took another twist. It reminded me of a "Primo Piatto" - a Pasta dish. Excellent taste all together.

- Sorbet & Herbs was a bit of a miss. Sorbet was frozen cold i.e. took some time to melt and the herbal tea did not fit

- Cham Island's Red Snapper - what an experience again. Perfect white fish mixed with smoked mushrooms etc. It reminded me of a forest. I would pair this with light red wine! Exquisite again

- Rack of lamb was simply perfect execution. The artichoke pyre mixed with the meat was terrific. A masterpiece.

- Dessert mix left also nothing to miss
